title: When Volatility Targeting Crowds — Quantifying the Tipping Point via ABM
summary: Paper is submission-ready. Reproduce.py runs clean in ~210s; 33/33 headline numbers match main.tex within <1% tolerance (100% match_rate). Seed robustness across 3 offsets (42, 13, 7) is high: VT Sharpe relative range <=19% at every adoption level, kurtosis spike at 70% (1.5-1.6) and 100% (62) directionally identical, AnnVol identical to 3 decimals. The '50-70% tipping point' range claim survives seed perturbation.

seed_robustness.method: Re-run k827v3 core simulation with 3 seed offsets (42=paper default, 13, 7), N_SIMS=120 per cell (reduced from 500 for runtime; still produces stable means)
seed_robustness.stability_verdict: All 3 seeds show identical qualitative pattern: flat Sharpe at 10-30%, ~30% decline at 50%, >80% collapse at 70%, negative at 100%. The paper's claim 'tipping point at 50-70%' is the RANGE spanning two adoption levels — so even though the knife-edge >30% rule flips '50%' vs '70%' across seeds, both values are INSIDE the paper's stated tipping range. No seed contradicts the paper narrative. Sharpe relative range <=19% << 30% stress threshold.

data_sources.md.note: Pure simulation - no external data dependencies

figures_directory.note: No includegraphics in main.tex - intentional (tabular paper)

minor_observations: results/README.md line 42 says 'Sharpe ~0.20 at 50%' but actual is 0.34. Cosmetic mismatch in secondary index file; main.tex and reproduce.py are correct. Not a blocking issue.
reproduce.py only verifies 2 t-stat claims; could be extended to check the full 33-cell matrix used in this audit. Not required for submission.
Seed 7 produces deg@50%=29.6% (below 30% threshold) vs seed 42/13 at ~37%. Paper's '50-70% range' wording already handles this correctly - no revision needed.
recommendation: APPROVE FOR SUBMISSION. alert_level=green. All 33 headline numbers match, 5 FRL hard requirements met, seed robustness confirms tipping-point claim within paper-stated range (50-70%). No (a)(b)(c) divergence action needed.
